basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 16.' and it opens '(Vers. 16.) Et audivit Abraham Ephron, et appendit Abraham Ephron argentum, quod locutus'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 16.) Et audivit Abraham Ephron, et appendit Abraham Ephron argentum, quod locutus est in auribus filiorum Heth. In Hebraeo sicut hic posuimus, primum nomen ejus scribitur EPHRON, secundum EPHRAN. Postquam enim pretio victus est, ut sepulcrum venderet argento, licet cogente Abraham, vau littera, quae apud illos pro o legitur, ablata de ejus nomine est: et pro EPHRON appellatus est EPHRAN, significante Scriptura, non eum fuisse consummatae perfectaeque virtutis, qui potuerit memorias vendere mortuorum. Sciant igitur, qui sepulcra venditant, et non coguntur, ut accipiant pretium, sed a nolentibus quoque extorquent, immutari nomen suum, et perire quid de merito eorum, cum etiam ille reprehendatur occulte, qui invitus acceperit.
